back door noun

classical

Traupman 122
Plaut.

postīcum, postīcī n.

noun, second declension

In Plautus, where rēctum ōstium is the front door.

Examples

  • pater et Theodōrus cum aviā per postīcum in hortum exiērunt

    Dad and Theo went out into the garden by the back door with GrandmaLibellus IV, Diēs Grātulātiōnis

See also front door, door.

SourcesLewis & Short: posticum

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 122, checked against the searchable text of the book (29 October 2026).
